title: Complex involutive normal forms and regularity propagation
source_hypothesis: Scalar ordinary PDO of order m with smooth homogeneous principal symbol modulo order m-1, independent real differentials at zero, involutive zero set and nonradial characteristic leaf. Arbitrary ordinary scalar lower terms are retained. Barrier s is superharmonic on a leaf open set and bounded above by the source regularity index.
reviewed_arguments: The exact scalar hypotheses are independent real principal differentials, involutivity on the zero set and independence of the two Hamilton fields with dilation. Radial and symplectic boundary cases are excluded explicitly.

The current FN:I0–I10 proof supplies a nonzero degree 1-m multiplier and an actual homogeneous canonical map, with n at least three. Its Hamilton equation identifies the intrinsic complex leaf structure.
The fundamental solution i/(2 pi z) has the correct sign for D1+iD2=-2i bar-partial. The compact-source planar solver preserves every ordinary symbol derivative on one fixed domain.

The full scalar exponential gauge is uniformly elliptic after extension. Full residual symbols have one fixed compact output support and the same solver removes them successively, without assuming a classical lower-order expansion.

Ordinary summation and two-sided elliptic inversion give the complete smoothing intertwiner. The exact graph order 1-m gives the source regularity shift m-1; no endpoint Sobolev membership is assumed.
The compact distribution inverse uses the locally integrable kernel restricted to a finite disk. The proof never claims globally bounded whole-plane convolution by 1/z on L2.

The disk localization retains a boundary collar, one common angular cone and transverse neighborhood, both cutoff terms, separated-kernel errors and smooth low frequencies. Distributions are never restricted to a leaf.
Harmonic conjugates, holomorphic polynomial approximation, general-domain comparison, the Poisson mean characterization and conformal invariance are proved in the receiving lesson.
The annular logarithmic minorant proves propagation of an infinite open set through a finite chain of leaf disks, with its boundary limitation explicit.
All variable-order symbol derivatives are estimated in local ordinary classes. The inverse-weight product gains 1-delta orders and has an actual asymptotic parametrix.
Holomorphicity makes the differential commutator vanish before cutoffs. Strict margins select attained Sobolev orders; the microlocal disk principle and inverse weight prove superharmonic comparison.

The smooth-wavefront corollary uses nearby leaves, an open ambient microlocal region, ellipticity off the characteristic set and one fixed cutoff for all Sobolev orders. Infinite index at a single point is not equated with microlocal smoothness.

Nineteen exact identities, 311 formulae, 24 displays, eleven overlapping desktop captures, one complete figure and two mobile samples support the review. Three complete exercises check the gauge sign, holomorphic commutator and annular bound.

This proves the scalar normal form, H4 Theorem 26.2.1 and Corollary 26.2.2. Prescribed superharmonic regularity, later Chapter 26 sections and all remaining course obligations stay active. The 102 human foundation proofs remain explicitly external.
